scenario.topic: Choose the game engine for the student game project

options.name: Unity Game Engine

attrs.supported_platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, Web
attrs.learning_resources: Extensive official tutorials and community forums

options.upside: Widely used with a large community and many learning materials.
options.concern: Can have a steep learning curve for beginners.

options.name: Unreal Engine

attrs.supported_platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, Consoles

options.upside: Strong for high-quality 3D graphics and visual scripting options.
options.concern: More complex interface and resource-intensive for smaller projects.

options.name: Godot Engine

attrs.supported_platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, Web

options.upside: Open-source with a lightweight interface and flexible scripting.
options.concern: Smaller community and fewer third-party assets compared to others.

options.name: GameMaker Studio 2
options.upside: Simplified 2D development with an easy-to-learn scripting language.
options.concern: Limited 3D capabilities and fewer export options for consoles.

shared_context: A group of seven students must select a game engine for their collaborative project. The engine should support 2D and 3D development, have accessible learning resources, and allow deployment on multiple platforms.

personas.name: Maya
personas.background: Maya is a computer science student passionate about versatile game development.
personas.private_goal: Choose an engine with strong community support to ease learning.

A.reason_for: Unity supports both 2D and 3D with extensive tutorials and a large community.

B.reason_for: Unreal offers high-fidelity 3D and visual scripting, which is appealing.
B.reason_against: Its complexity and resource demands might slow down our project.

C.reason_for: Godot is lightweight and open-source with flexible scripting options.
C.reason_against: Smaller community and fewer assets could limit support.

D.reason_against: Limited 3D support and fewer platform exports reduce versatility.

personas.name: Liam
personas.background: Liam is an experienced coder focused on high-quality 3D graphics.
personas.private_goal: Select the engine best suited for advanced 3D visuals and VR potential.

A.reason_for: Unity supports 3D and multiple platforms with a strong community.
A.reason_against: It may not match Unreal’s high-fidelity graphics.

B.reason_for: Unreal excels at high-quality 3D and VR with powerful scripting options.

C.reason_for: Godot offers 3D support and is lightweight.
C.reason_against: It lacks the polish and resources of Unreal or Unity.

D.reason_for: GameMaker is easy to use for 2D but limited for 3D needs.
D.reason_against: It does not support high-fidelity 3D or consoles well.

personas.name: Zara
personas.background: Zara is a creative student interested in flexible and open-source tools.
personas.private_goal: Find an engine that balances ease of use with scripting flexibility.

A.reason_for: Unity’s extensive resources and 2D/3D support fit our needs well.

B.reason_for: Unreal is powerful but too complex and resource-intensive for us.
B.reason_against: Its complexity outweighs benefits for our project scale.

C.reason_for: Godot is open-source and flexible with multiple scripting languages.
C.reason_against: Smaller community might limit help and assets.

D.reason_for: GameMaker is beginner-friendly and good for 2D projects.

personas.name: Noah
personas.background: Noah is focused on quick development with beginner-friendly tools.
personas.private_goal: Pick an engine that allows easy 2D game creation and fast learning.

A.reason_for: Unity supports both 2D and 3D with many learning resources.
A.reason_against: Steep learning curve may slow us down.

B.reason_for: Unreal is powerful but too complex and resource-heavy for quick projects.
B.reason_against: Its complexity is a barrier for beginners.

C.reason_for: Godot is lightweight and supports 2D and 3D.

D.reason_for: GameMaker Studio is easy to learn and great for 2D development.

personas.name: Eva
personas.background: Eva is a graphics enthusiast who values high-end visuals and performance.
personas.private_goal: Use the most powerful engine for impressive 3D graphics.

A.reason_for: Unity offers solid 3D capabilities and wide platform support.
A.reason_against: Not as graphically advanced as Unreal.

B.reason_for: Unreal Engine’s high-fidelity 3D and VR support are unmatched.

C.reason_against: Lacks the advanced graphics features of Unreal or Unity.

D.reason_for: GameMaker is easy but limited to 2D and fewer platforms.

personas.name: Omar
personas.background: Omar is a detail-oriented student who prefers thorough explanations and discussion.
personas.private_goal: Ensure the engine is easy to learn and suitable for 2D projects.

A.reason_for: Unity has extensive tutorials and supports both 2D and 3D.
A.reason_against: Learning curve might be steep for some.

B.reason_for: Unreal is powerful but complex and resource-intensive.
B.reason_against: Too advanced for our current skill level.

D.reason_for: GameMaker Studio is beginner-friendly with good 2D support.

personas.name: Nia
personas.background: Nia is a pragmatic student who values directness and efficiency in tools.
personas.private_goal: Pick an engine that balances ease of use with powerful features.

A.reason_for: Unity supports 2D and 3D with a large community and many tutorials.

B.reason_for: Unreal offers great graphics but is complex and resource-heavy.
B.reason_against: Not ideal for smaller or less experienced teams.

C.reason_for: Godot is flexible and lightweight with growing community support.
C.reason_against: Fewer assets and tutorials compared to Unity.

D.reason_for: GameMaker is simple and good for 2D projects.
